summary: A comparative overview of how popular esports titles such as League of Legends, Dota 2, CS:GO, Fortnite, Overwatch, Call of Duty and others build and sustain their communities. It covers tournaments, prize pools, platforms, content creators, social media, inclusivity initiatives and sponsorships. The note concludes that each game tailors its engagement strategy to its audience, but the shared goal is to engage and grow the community.
one_line: Comparative analysis of how major esports titles cultivate communities through tournaments, platforms, creators, social media, inclusivity and sponsorships.
key_facts: The International, the Dota 2 tournament, had a crowdfunded prize pool (via in-game purchases) that reached $40 million in September 2023.
In October 2023, Fortnite's World Cup event brought together solo players and cooperative squad tactics.
Blizzard's Overwatch League uses global teams representing different cities to encourage local loyalty.
League of Legends is developed by Riot Games, whose community includes streamers like Michael "Imaqtpie" Santana, pros, cosplayers, artists and casual fans.
The Dota 2 community prizes a high skill ceiling and complex strategy; Valve Corporation fosters it by facilitating modding, and figures like Kuro "KuroKy" Takhasomi advocate for its depth.
Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, from Valve, has a veteran, tight-knit community including Christopher "GeT_RiGhT" Alesund.
Epic Games released Fortnite on practically every platform, and its cross-play bridges PC and console gamers.
Call of Duty launched Warzone, a free-to-play battle royale mode, which attracted players like Jack "CouRage" Dunlop with an established audience.
On November 12, 2023, an underdog team won the League of Legends championship cup.
Markiplier (Mark Fischbach) energized Minecraft's esports scene with mod competitions and building contests, while Roblox's community doubles as developers.
Twitter, Reddit and Discord serve as connective tissue for esports fans.
Inclusivity efforts include Overwatch celebrating Pride Month and female and LGBTQ+ tournaments in CS:GO; a landmark inclusivity event with global leaders took place at the end of September 2023.
Adidas announced a deal with Tyler "Ninja" Blevins in August 2023, illustrating the commercial role of sponsorships.
